title: Eugene Emeralds
content: ## Eugene Emeralds. The **Eugene Emeralds** (nicknamed the Ems) are a Minor League Baseball team in the northwest United States, based in Eugene, Oregon. The Emeralds are members of the Northwest League and the High-A affiliate of the San Francisco Giants. The Emeralds were the first minor-league team to play in Eugene since the disbanding of the Eugene Larks, who played at Bethel Park for just two seasons, 1950 and 1951. In 1950 and 1951, Bethel Park was the home of the Eugene Larks of the Class D Far West League); its outfield is present-day Lark Park. Facing an outdated stadium and high-maintenance costs, in 2010 the Eugene Emeralds moved into PK Park, the new baseball stadium across town that was built by the University of Oregon. In the winter of 2020 as part the reorganization of minor league baseball, Eugene received an invitation to play as the High-A affiliate of San Francisco Giants.

content: San Francisco Giants Team Logo. # Explore Eugene's PK Park. Welcome to Eugene's PK Park, where Giants play before they're fully grown. **Eugene Emeralds** (High-A affiliate of the San Francisco Giants since 2021). The Emeralds -- or Ems, for short -- haven't played in the NWL for the entirety of their existence, however, as from 1969-73 they were members of the Triple-A Pacific Coast League. In 2021, the same year in which the Emeralds' affiliation with the Giants began, the NWL was reclassified as a High-A (full-season) league. PK Park is located north (and across the Willamette River) from the University of Oregon's campus, in the shadow of gargantuan Autzen Stadium. When the Emeralds switched classifications and became a full-season team in 2021, they joined the Ducks baseball team in playing games in April and May. PK Park is therefore an exceedingly busy facility, and the Ems' longer-term goal is to move into a ballpark built specially for them.

title: Section 4 football stadiums named after NY coaches, icons
content: # Why is U-E's stadium named after Ty Cobb? This plaque honoring Joseph Brewer appears at Elmira Notre Dame's Brewer Memorial Stadium. ## Brewer Memorial Stadium, Elmira Notre Dame. Edward Joseph Brewer was a football, basketball and baseball standout at Notre Dame High School, but the school's decision to name its stadium for him was largely about contributions to his country. Brewer Memorial Stadium is named in his honor. Brewer, a member of Notre Dame's class of 1964, was killed Feb. 6, 1968 while serving as a U.S. Marine in the Vietnam War. Following his death, he was awarded the Purple Heart, Navy Achievement Medal and Vietnamese Cross of Gallantry. Harold Vernon Cobb, known to many as Ty, was one of the most successful high school coaches in Section 4 history. Cobb, who coached at Corning before settling in at Union-Endicott, was U-E's athletic director and introduced junior varsity football to the school.
